newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU farm ministers reject Irish beef plan.
newsitem.headline: EU farm ministers reject Irish beef plan.

text.p: European Union farm ministers unanimously rejected a compromise plan on Tuesday to break a deadlock over measures to cut output and compensate beef farmers battered by the mad cow crisis, EU officials said.
But Ireland, current holder of the EU Presidency, was preparing a fresh compromise to present around 1900/1700 GMT.
"Our intention is to keep trying to get an agreement," an Irish official said, adding talks could go through the night.
The European Commission said success looked remote.
"It's very difficult to see how we can get an agreement," said Gerard Kiely, Commission agriculture spokesman.
"Ministers are trying to spend money which doesn't exist. They are not dealing with the central problem of reducing output."
Ireland had suggested postponing cuts in aid to cereals farmers to help fund the beef package as well as easing a politically unpalatable reduction in production.

But member states complained that the aid plans were too vague and disagreed over how production should be cut following a 15 percent drop in beef demand since the scare over Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) broke in March.
"The draft compromise is unacceptable. It's even provocative," said French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur.
Vasseur said Paris would reject any compromise that did not compensate beef producers for income losses due to BSE.
Most member states rejected key Commission measures to cut output, notably the so-called "Herod premium" for slaughtering new born calves, saying it would stir public outrage.
But ministers were divided over weight limits and other details of alternative German short-term measures to promote marketing of young cattle.
